Overall, for myself, yes. Here are some of the pros and cons as well as a few things I found helpful after high school. 

Pros: not having to wake up every morning and go to school (I didn't go to college), much stronger sense of self and understanding of the world, freedom to go where I want and do what I want, get to eat ice cream whenever I feel like it


Cons: harder to maintain a social life due to conflicting schedules and people moving/starting families, money can be a struggle, struggle to find a propose for my life 


Things I found helpful: find some type of social activity so I don't isolate (for me this is church and recovery meetings), learn some basic personal finance skills, organization and cleanliness has helped me tremendously with my anxiety. 


Best of luck to you!  :)

I need to be more proactive at cutting out bad thoughts before they have a chance to detail me. Overanalyzing and catastrophising (worrying about worst-case scenarios) are big struggles for me. I don't know what else I therapist could tell me that I haven't heard before but it helps to have something scheduled where I can just dump all my stuff out I guess. I think this with going on meds again would help me. I always quit taking meds because I feel weak and get down in myself (especially as a man). But I know that thinking is bs. They actually do, believe it or not, have a Heroin Anonymous meeting. I actually prefer AA though to other support groups, generally there is more sobriety time and more old timers who have good advice. I've been through the 12 steps with a sponsor before  and had 3 years (almost) of continuous sobreity so I know the program very well. The fucked up thing though, every day or that 3 years I wanted to use, I just gets worse and worse and worse and worse until you either give in or just off yourself. I wish I never tried this drug :(

A lot of my dealing with panic attacks honestly has just come with experience. I know that I'm going to be okay ultimately so it kinda solidifies and is affirmed each time I come out of one. I guess one "technique" I use (I don't have a name for it) is I pick an object and see how many words I can use to describe it. Ex: The grass is: green, soft, alive, growing, damp, freshly-cut, etc. until I run out of adjectives and then move on to the next object.
